title: Local existence and codimension calculus for dimension functions
statement: Let $T$ be a Noetherian universally catenary scheme, meaning that every affine coordinate ring is Noetherian and every finite-type algebra over it is catenary in the bounded saturated-chain sense of [def-exc-excellent-ring]. A dimension function is a function $\delta:|T|\to\mathbf Z$ such that $\delta(v)-\delta(w)=1$ for every immediate geometric specialization $\bar v\rightsquigarrow\bar w$; immediate means that the reduced closure of $\bar v$ in $T_{(\bar w)}$ has Krull dimension one [def-weil-geometric-point, def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Dimension functions exist Zariski locally on $T$; in particular a Noetherian universally catenary local scheme admits one on the whole scheme. For any dimension function $\delta$ and any geometric specialization $\bar v\rightsquigarrow\bar w$, one has $\delta(v)-\delta(w)=c_T(\bar v,\bar w)$, where $c_T$ is the Krull dimension of that reduced closure in $T_{(\bar w)}$. This equality also holds for identity specializations and geometric isomorphisms, with codimension zero.
